newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates firmer in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates firmer in slow trade.

text.p: Term loans pushed up Croatian money market rates in very slow trade on Tuesday amid continued high liquidity, dealers said.
"We've had an exceptionally low daily trade of 6.25 million kuna," one dealer said.
"Accounts are good so only banks which wanted term loans struck some deals," she said.
Banks' accounts rose to 633 million from Monday's 548 million, the dealer added.
Call money deals, which usually make up most of the trading, were not made on Tuesday.
A one-week loan was granted to a savings bank at 15 percent. One-month loans were struck at 30 percent while two- and three-month borrowings were granted at 18 percent.
Two banks sought 11.2 million kuna on Monday night -- one to maintain its mandatory reserve and the other to square its position.
Banks had 14.2 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, up from Monday's 6.57 million.
Monday's reserve payment drained 3.38 billion kuna from the system, or 35.1 million more than a fortnight ago. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
